title: EU data-lock routing and tier-aware fallback model mapping
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Purpose: Implement a deterministic Enforcement Path for EU-only and data-residency contracts that guarantees requests and derived KV/prefix cache remain within allowed regions and customer allowlists. This ticket defines the control-plane policy model, runtime enforcement hooks, tier-aware routing behavior, and safe fallback mapping to compatible model variants when the primary model or region is unavailable.

Background: Several enterprise contracts require strict EU residency or an allowlist of regions for particular customers. Current smart routing supports regional preference but lacks a single, auditable flow that combines: (a) per-customer region allowlists/denylists, (b) tier routing (free/hosted/dedicated), and (c) fallback model variant selection that preserves residency guarantees and acceptable latency/cost tradeoffs.

Goals:
- Define a policy model that can express EU-only (hard residency), region allowlist/denylist, and per-route tier constraints.
- Ensure policy is enforced at both the control plane (routing decision) and the data plane (runtime execution, cache locality, and logging).
- Create deterministic fallback model mapping rules that never violate residency allowlists (e.g., fallback variants must be region-compatible).
- Provide an audit trail and metrics for compliance verification and SLO reporting.

Key design decisions and trade-offs: 
1) Control-plane policy vs data-plane enforcement: primary enforcement will be control-plane routing so traffic is never routed to disallowed regions. The data-plane will include defensive checks (reject or redirect) in case of drift or misrouting. Trade-off: more latency at routing time for policy evaluation vs stronger upfront guarantees. We accept small routing latency increase for stronger compliance contracts.

2) Allowlist vs Denylist semantics: per-customer settings support both. Allowlist is authoritative (only listed regions allowed). Denylist is advisory but aggregated with global constraints. Implementation: store canonical allowlist per-tenant and merge with product-level restrictions.

3) Tier-aware routing: Customers may require Dedicated or Private; hosted tier requests may be routed to dedicated pools if allowed and capacity exists. When capacity is exhausted, fallback must respect residency — the system will attempt (ordered): (a) another dedicated pool in allowed regions, (b) private deployment in allowed region (if customer owns one), (c) hosted-compatible model pinned to EU-only variant. If none available, route to error with clear customer-facing error code describing compliance block.

4) Fallback model variant selection: fallback candidates must be flagged as "region-compatible" and have an equivalence score threshold (default 0.85) to avoid unacceptable regressions. Quantization or smaller models can be used only if they execute within allowed regions.

5) Cache residency: persistent KV/prefix caches must be colocated with execution and respect residency constraints. If a request would read a cached prefix from an off-region store, the system must deny cache hit and either re-execute in-region or return a miss.

Acceptance criteria: see acceptance_criteria list.

Deliverables:
- Policy schema additions (allowlist/denylist, residency_mode: {SOFT, HARD}, tier_constraints, fallback_map).
- Control-plane evaluator that produces a routing decision object with traceable policy tags.
- Runtime enforcement hooks (cache access policy, region check).
- Fallback resolver service that selects region-compatible model variants and emits reason codes.
- End-to-end tests and a staged rollout to selected EU enterprise customers.

Security & compliance notes: KMS/HSM keys and logs for audit must be retained in-region according to customer contract. This feature requires security review and certification before GA.
acceptance_criteria: Policy schema stored in config service; supports per-tenant allowlist and denylist
Control-plane routing returns only allowed regions for tenants with residency_mode=HARD
Runtime rejects or reroutes any execution attempt outside allowed regions and logs event with policy tag
Fallback resolver never selects a model variant that violates tenant allowlist
End-to-end integration tests that simulate region outage and verify correct fallback and error codes
Audit logs available for 90 days in-region and accessible to compliance team
implementation_notes: Schema: add fields to /config/tenants/{id}: residency_mode, region_allowlist, region_denylist, tier_requirements, fallback_preferences. Control-plane: extend routing evaluator to query tenant config and capacity index; implement short-circuit for HARD residency. Runtime: add middleware layer before model invocation to validate exec_region==allowed; instrument cache layer to tag cache objects with region and tenant. Fallback resolver: use candidate pool filtered by region and equivalence score; emit structured fallback_reason codes (e.g., FALLBACK_REGION_UNAVAILABLE, FALLBACK_CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED, FALLBACK_NO_COMPATIBLE_VARIANT).
rollout_plan: Implement schema and control-plane evaluator behind feature flag (runtime flag: geo_policy_v2)
Unit tests + integration tests in staging with synthetic EU-only tenant
Canary rollout to 5 EU enterprise customers with support on-call
Enable for all tenants with opt-in; enforce for contracted tenants after security sign-off
GA after 4 weeks of canary and compliance verification
telemetry_and_metrics: metric.routing.decisions.total{policy=geo} (count of routing decisions filtered by policy)
metric.cache.miss_due_to_residency (count of cache misses caused by residency enforcement)
SLO: 99.9% of compliant requests must return decision within 80ms at control-plane evaluation
